[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Define speed.","marks":1,"answer":"Speed is the rate of change of distance with respect to time.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"The motion of a clock is periodic but not harmonic–explain.","marks":2,"answer":"If the motion of a moving object passes repeatedly through a definite point in the same direction in the same manner in a definite interval of time, then this motion is called periodic motion. The hands of a clock rotate at a fixed speed, so, their motion is periodic. If an object in periodic motion spends half of its motion in a certain direction and the other half in the same path in opposite direction, it is called harmonic motion. But the hands of a clock do not change their direction, therefore, they are not in harmonic motion.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Calculate the distance of the moving body in 19th second.","marks":3,"answer":"The 19th second falls in the deceleration phase (after t = 15 seconds).
At t = 15 s, velocity = 15 m/s
Deceleration = \(\frac{15 - 0}{4} = 3.75 \, \text{ms}^{-2}\)
At t = 18 s (start of 19th second), velocity = \(15 - 3.75 \times 3 = 3.75 \, \text{ms}^{-1}\)
At t = 19 s (end of 19th second), velocity = \(15 - 3.75 \times 4 = 0 \, \text{ms}^{-1}\)
Distance in 19th second = average velocity × time
\[= \frac{3.75 + 0}{2} \times 1 = 1.875 \, \text{m}\]
(Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"According to given stem draw force time graph of OABC part.","marks":4,"answer":"Force during acceleration phase (0-10 s):

Force during constant velocity phase (10-15 s):
\[F = 0 \, \text{N}\]
Force during deceleration phase (15-19 s):
\[F = ma = 15 \times (-3.75) = -56.25 \, \text{N}\]
The force-time graph would show a horizontal line at 22.5 N from 0-10 s, then drop to 0 N from 10-15 s, then drop to -56.25 N from 15-19 s.

Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"A p-n diode is called a rectifier because it allows current to flow in one direction only and blocks it in the opposite direction.
In a p-n diode, the p-side (positive) and n-side (negative) create a junction with a depletion region. When a forward voltage is applied (positive to p-side and negative to n-side), the diode conducts electricity. However, when a reverse voltage is applied, the depletion region widens, preventing current flow. This property of allowing current to flow only in one direction is called rectification, which is why the p-n diode is used as a rectifier in converting alternating current (AC) to direct current (DC).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Determine the value and direction of the velocities of the two objects after the collision.","marks":3,"answer":"For elastic collision, we use:
\[v_1 = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)u_1 + 2m_2u_2}{m_1 + m_2}\]
\[v_2 = \frac{(m_2 - m_1)u_2 + 2m_1u_1}{m_1 + m_2}\]
Here, \(m_1 = 200\) kg, \(u_1 = 5.5\) ms\(^{-1}\), \(m_2 = 400\) kg, \(u_2 = 1\) ms\(^{-1}\)
\[v_1 = \frac{(200 - 400) \times 5.5 + 2 \times 400 \times 1}{200 + 400}\]
\[= \frac{-1100 + 800}{600} = \frac{-300}{600} = -0.5 \, \text{ms}^{-1}\]
\[v_2 = \frac{(400 - 200) \times 1 + 2 \times 200 \times 5.5}{600}\]
\[= \frac{200 + 2200}{600} = \frac{2400}{600} = 4 \, \text{ms}^{-1}\]
After collision, the first car moves at 0.5 ms\(^{-1}\) in the opposite direction, and the second car moves at 4 ms\(^{-1}\) in the original direction. (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Give a mathematical analysis of whether kinetic energy is conserved before and after the collision.","marks":4,"answer":"Kinetic energy before collision:
\[KE_i = \frac{1}{2}m_1u_1^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_2u_2^2\]
\[= \frac{1}{2} \times 200 \times 5.5^2 + \frac{1}{2} \times 400 \times 1^2\]
\[= 3025 + 200 = 3225 \, \text{J}\]
Kinetic energy after collision:
\[KE_f = \frac{1}{2}m_1v_1^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_2v_2^2\]
\[= \frac{1}{2} \times 200 \times 0.5^2 + \frac{1}{2} \times 400 \times 4^2\]
\[= 25 + 3200 = 3225 \, \text{J}\]
Since \(KE_i = KE_f\), kinetic energy is conserved. This confirms it is an elastic collision. (Ans.)

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"Write down the Galileo's 3rd law.","marks":1,"answer":"Galileo's \(3^{rd}\) law: The distance (h) traversed by a freely falling body from rest in a given time (t) is directly proportional to the square of the given time, i. e., h \(\propto\) t\(^2\).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why do the passengers lean backward when a stopped bus suddenly starts moving?","marks":2,"answer":"When a stationary car suddenly starts moving, the passengers lean backward due to Newton's First Law of Motion, which states that an object at rest tends to stay at rest. Initially, the passengers were at rest, and when the car accelerates forward, their bodies want to remain at rest. As a result, they lean backward as their bodies resist the change in motion, creating the sensation of being pushed back into their seats. This effect is a manifestation of inertia, where objects resist changes in their state of motion unless acted upon by an external force.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Find the combined velocity of the both cars after the collisions.","marks":3,"answer":"Similar to the creative question-answer 12 (c).
Ans: 3.23 ms\(^{-1}\), on the direction of the car.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Did it reach to the destination? Find mathematically.","marks":4,"answer":"At first, the car started from rest and moved in uniform acceleration of 2 ms\(^{-2}\) for 7 sec.
So, v = u + at = 0 + 2x7 = 14 ms\(^{-1}\)
\[s_1 = 0 \times 7 + \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 7^2 = 49 \, \text{m}\]
Then it moved in constant velocity for 1 min.
\[\dot{s}_2 = vt = 14 \times 60 = 840 \, \text{m}\]
Finally it collided with a truck and stopped after 15 s. The velocity of the car after collision, v = 3.23 ms\(^{-1}\) [From 'c']
Now, v\(^2\) = u\(^2\) + 2as\(_3\)
Here, a = \(\frac{v - u}{t} = \frac{0 - 3.23}{15} = -0.215 \, \text{ms}^{-2}\)
So, s\(_3\) = \(\frac{v^2 - u^2}{2a} = \frac{0^2 - 3.23^2}{2 \times (-0.215)} = 24.26 \, \text{m}\)
Total distance, s = s\(_1\) + s\(_2\) + s\(_3\) = 49 + 840 + 24.26 = 913.26 m
As the destination was 1000 m, the car could not make it to the destination.

When we walk, we exert a force on the ground. According to Newton’s 3rd law, the ground also applies an equal and opposite force on our body. Therefore, the reaction force is less and we face trouble while walking on sand.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"After how long will there be a collision between them?","marks":3,"answer":"Let, the cars will collide with each other at x distance in the same time.
Here,
The velocity of the loaded car, \( v_1 = 12 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)
The velocity of the empty car, \( v_2 = 20 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)
The distance between them = 800 m
Let,
The loaded car travelled, \( s_1 = x \, \text{m} \)
The empty car travelled, \( s_2 = (800 - x) \, \text{m} \)
Here,
The loaded car goes 12 m in 1 s
∴ The loaded car goes 1 m in \(\frac{1}{12} s\)
∴ The loaded car goes x m in \(\frac{1 \times x}{12} = \frac{x}{12} s\)
Again,
The empty car goes 20 m in 1 s
∴ The empty car goes 1 m in \(\frac{1}{20} s\)
∴ The empty car goes \((800 - x) \, \text{m}\) in \(\frac{1 \times (800 - x)}{20} = \frac{800 - x}{20} s\)
Now,
\[\frac{x}{12} = \frac{800 - x}{20}\]
\[\Rightarrow 20x = 9600 - 12x\]
\[\Rightarrow 20x + 12x = 9600\]
\[\Rightarrow 32x = 9600\]
∴ x = 300 m
∴ The cars will collide after \(\frac{300}{12} = 25 \, \text{s}\). (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Which of the two cars will be more damaged? Explain it mathematically.","marks":4,"answer":"The one with the higher momentum will apply more impact force, thus inflicting more damage to the other car.
Given,
The loaded car’s mass, \( m_1 = 12000 \, \text{kg} \)
The empty car’s mass, \( m_2 = 800 \, \text{kg} \)
The loaded car’s velocity, \( v_1 = 12 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)
The empty car’s velocity, \( v_2 = 20 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)
The loaded car’s momentum, \( p_1 = m_1 v_1 \)
\[= (12000 \times 12) \, \text{kgms}^{-1}\]
\[= 144000 \, \text{kgms}^{-1}\]
The empty car’s momentum, \( p_2 = m_2 v_2 \)
\[= (800 \times 20) \, \text{kgms}^{-1}\]
\[= 16000 \, \text{kgms}^{-1}\]
Here, \( p_1 >> p_2 \). So, the empty car will be more damaged by the loaded car.
